content.title: About
content.content: Parsley (Petroselinum crispum) is an annual herb widely used as a culinary garnish. Fresh parsley has bright green leaves, a fragrant, slightly bitter taste and a crisp texture. It is eaten raw, added to salads, soups, sauces and as a garnish for many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Parsley belongs to the Apiaceae family and is closely related to celery and dill.
There are two main varieties: curly leaf and flat‑leaf (Italian), the latter being more flavorful.
In ancient Roman medicine parsley was used as a breath freshener.
Its high chlorophyll content makes it a popular addition to detox smoothies.
Parsley is sometimes credited with mild diuretic properties.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Fresh parsley provides over 100 % of the daily value of vitamin C per 100 g, supporting immune function and antioxidant defense.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health; parsley supplies more than 600 % of the DV per 100 g.

items.title: Folate source
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Parsley contains flavonoids such as quercetin and kaempferol, as well as carotenoids, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It provides potassium, iron and magnesium, supporting heart and muscle function.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to parsley, ranging from skin itching to swelling.

items.title: High vitamin K intake
items.content: Because of its vitamin K content, excessive consumption may interfere with anticoagulant medication.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Parsley contains oxalates, which in large amounts can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use fresh parsley by chopping it into salads, sauces (pesto, gremolata), soups, omelets and smoothies. It can be sprinkled over finished dishes for color and flavor. For a milder taste, briefly blanch the leaves.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh parsley in the refrigerator in a damp paper towel or in a glass of water covered with plastic wrap. It stays fresh for 5‑7 days. For longer storage, chop and freeze the leaves in airtight bags.
